title: Augmented ordered localization model of the Godement ring complex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset A$ a finitely generated ideal. Assume the ordinary derived category $D(A)$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] in the indicated universe. The actual augmented Godement mapping fibre $(K(A,I),\epsilon_{A,I})$ of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-godement-construction] satisfies $\operatorname{RingComplexHasCechModel}(A,I,K(A,I),\epsilon_{A,I})$ of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data]. Thus every finite generating list, including the empty list, gives the precise ordered product-localization coordinates, alternating differential, negative-degree vanishing and degree-zero identity augmentation, together with an augmentation-compatible isomorphism to $K(A,I)$ in $D(A)$.

proof.text: For a list f spanning I, cover the open complement by the principal opens D(f_i). Each ordered intersection is D(product f_i) and is affine; its structure-module sections are the corresponding localization. The restriction maps are the unique algebra maps between those localizations.

The specified Godement augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism and its terms are flasque. On each affine intersection the structure module has vanishing positive cohomology, while every Godement term is acyclic for sections. The bounded-below acyclic-resolution comparison therefore makes the section augmentation a quasi-isomorphism.

Apply the finite ordered flasque-Cech comparison, giving a roof between Godement global sections and the finite localization Cech complex through its double total, with the degree-zero augmentation square. Take mapping fibres of the maps from A[0]. Identity on A and quasi-isomorphism on sections give quasi-isomorphism on fibres by the long exact homology sequence. The localization fibre has the requested coordinates; change the signs of successive positive-degree coordinates to match the inverse-rotation convention. The projection is identity on A. Invert this roof in D(A), retaining the augmentation square. For r=0 the open is empty, the section complexes vanish and the same fibre is A[0]; zero and repeated generators and the zero ring use these same formulas.
